messages:
IncidentBot: Pager: high 5xx rate from region me-south1 -> egress gateway pool A. AlertID: IB-229876. Automated mitigations attempted: failed to reroute (code 502).
Alex (on-call): Saw it. I'm jumping in. Quick summary? which customers impacted?
Jin (sre): CPU fine on nodes, connections to peering provider are seeing resets. TCP retransmit spike from 10:03 -> 10:08 UTC.
Maya (netops): Confirming peering flap. External provider reported maintenance, but we didn't get prior comms. BGP withdraws for a subset of prefixes.
Priya (eng-runtime): Runtime shows dropped egress connections for active qps -> 30% of me-south1 requests. KV-cache hits normal. Not a model issue.
Alex (on-call): Ok. Priority = P1 (customer visible). Start mitigation plan: 1) divert new sessions from me-south1 to me-north1 fallback cluster for non-data-sensitive traffic 2) engage provider 3) status page draft and customer notification.
Alex (on-call): @DeployBot trigger canary reroute of traffic for region me-south1 -> me-north1 using traffic-router policy 'egress-fallback-v2'. Keep TTL 60s.
DeployBot: Canary reroute started: traffic-router apply --policy egress-fallback-v2 --region me-south1 --pct 10 --ttl 60
Jin (sre): Monitoring: canary 10% successful, but some sessions pinned to cache keys still hitting me-south1. Need to invalidate prefix cache for affected model routes. Priya can you invalidate prefix cache for /chat and /generate for me-south1?
Priya (eng-runtime): Running prefix invalidation:
```
POST /internal/cache/invalidate
{"region":"me-south1","routes":["/v1/chat","/v1/generate"],"reason":"egress peering flap"}
```
Invalidation submitted, propagation ~15s.
Maya (netops): Provider acknowledgement: ticket #PROV-7832 opened. They show noisy interface on edge router B, RFO: suspected upstream capacity shift. They will hold BGP session but limit prefixes until 10:30 UTC.
Alex (on-call): Customer impact assessment: approx 8% of production requests degrade to error or latency > 2s. Most traffic is retrying and falling back to me-north1 after canary increase. Affected customers: a subset of customers with region pinned workloads in AP/ME.
Jin (sre): Actionables: 1) escalate with provider (Maya) 2) continue canary ramp to 50% if stable 3) craft statuspage update 4) prepare customer notification for enterprise-comm.
Alex (on-call): I'll prepare the internal comm and status page draft. Priya, set canary to 25% now.
Priya (eng-runtime): traffic-router set --policy egress-fallback-v2 --region me-south1 --pct 25 --reason "me-south1 peering flap"
Traffic now 25% diverted. No error spike on fallback cluster.
Jin (sre): Telemetry: errors from me-south1 decreasing proportionally. Still seeing ~2% pinned sessions that need manual session transfer.
Alex (on-call): Draft status page (please review):

[STATUS PAGE DRAFT]
Component: egress gateway - me-south1
Impact: Partial service degradation for traffic originating in me-south1. Some requests may see increased latency or 5xx errors.
Current status: Mitigation in progress - traffic is being partially routed to me-north1 fallback cluster.
Timeline: 10:02 UTC - Alerts triggered; 10:05 UTC - mitigation started (10% canary); 10:12 UTC - prefix cache invalidation; 10:18 UTC - canary increased to 25%.
Next update: 10:45 UTC or sooner if status changes.

Alex (on-call): Draft customer notification for impacted customers (enterprise style):

Subject: Temporary service degradation for requests via me-south1 (Oct 12, 10:02 UTC)
Hi <Customer>,
We are investigating a partial degradation affecting requests routed through our me-south1 egress gateways. We have implemented an automated reroute to our me-north1 fallback cluster which has restored service for the majority of traffic. You may see increased latency or occasional 5xx responses while we finish mitigation.
What we are doing: working with our upstream peering provider to restore stable egress routing, increasing reroute coverage, and validating customer sessions to minimize retries.
Estimated next update: 10:45 UTC.
If you rely on region-pinned routing for compliance, please reach out to your account rep and we can coordinate tighter controls.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Incident Response

Maya (netops): Provider updated: doing long-lived BGP flap mitigation, may take until 10:40 UTC. They advise to avoid increasing full traffic cutover until stability confirmed.
Jin (sre): Recommendation: ramp canary to 50% but hold at 50% until BGP sessions stable. We should also open a targeted support thread for customers with region lock requirements.
Priya (eng-runtime): Implementing session-handoff for pinned sessions: running session-transfer job for active session IDs where possible. Command: 
```
POST /internal/session/transfer
{"from_region":"me-south1","to_region":"me-north1","max_concurrent":200}
```
Started - ETA ~5m.
Alex (on-call): I'll post the status page update now.
StatusBot: STATUS PAGE UPDATE POSTED: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/IB-229876 - "Partial degradation in me-south1 egress"
Alex (on-call): Sending customer notification bundle to Enterprise comms for review. Sam, I need you to take the next 30m handoff at 10:30 UTC in case I need to escalate.
Sam (next-oncall): On it. I'll monitor the dashboard and coordinate with Maya for provider comms.
Jin (sre): Current plan recap: 1) provider engagement + monitoring 2) ramp canary to 50% if stable at 10:25 UTC 3) continue session-transfer 4) prepare RCA draft once resolved.
Maya (netops): Provider says they will remove prefix limits at 10:39 UTC, will confirm BGP full convergence by 10:45 UTC.
Alex (on-call): Leaving thread to Sam for active follow-up. I'll join if escalation needed.
Sam (next-oncall): Acknowledged. Will update thread with any customer escalations and next status update at 10:45 or sooner.
